title: Fruit
description: Name the fruit, and get the plural right.
grammar: gender and articles, and the plural of nouns
grammarNote: Most fruit words are feminine, but the two big round ones are not.

explanation.summary: Fruit is a small, closed set of nouns that a learner meets very early, because it is what is in the kitchen and on the table. Nearly all of them are feminine.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: La manzana, la naranja, la sandía, la fresa, la cereza and la pera are all feminine. El plátano, el melón and el limón are masculine. La sandía is a good one to remember: it ends in -ía and keeps the feminine article, while el melón is masculine.

sections.heading: One grape and many
sections.body: Most fruit just adds -s or -es in the plural: las manzanas, los plátanos, las cerezas. One word does not: la uva becomes las uvas, and the -a drops. It is the commonest irregular plural in the language, and the only one you meet at this level.

items.note: Feminine: la naranja. The colour is also la naranja.
Feminine: la uva. The plural drops the -a: las uvas.

drills.note: The plural of uva drops the -a.
Pera is feminine, so una pera.
